extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in political economy, public finance, and military policy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for organizing, financing, and evaluating a state's military force (militia vs standing army), with attention to how social/economic structure and technology affect costs and effectiveness. Useful for assessing defense policy choices and their fiscal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary duty of the sovereign: protection from violence and invasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The first duty of the sovereign, that of protecting the society from the violence and invasion of other independent societies, can be performed only by means of a military force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes defense as a principal public expense; any evaluation of sovereign expenditures must begin from this duty and recognize that preparing and employing military force are unavoidable parts of state responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defence expense depends on the state's social and economic condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense both of preparing this military force in time of peace, and of employing it in time of war, is very different in the different states of society, in the different periods of improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish among hunters, shepherds, husbandmen, and manufacturing societies: hunters and some shepherds largely self-maintain in war; husbandmen can sometimes be spared without severe loss; artisans and manufacturers cannot, increasing the public cost. Policy evaluation must account for social composition when estimating defense burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two methods of providing public defence: militia or standing army
rubrics_metrics.description: It may either, first, by means of a very rigorous police... enforce the practice of military exercises (militia). Or, secondly, by maintaining and employing a certain number of citizens in the constant practice of military exercises, it may render the trade of a soldier a particular trade (standing army).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending or assessing a defence scheme, weigh enforcement and civic-training measures for militias against the fiscal and institutional costs of professional soldiers maintained by the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia: characteristics and inherent limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of military exercises is only the occasional occupation of the soldiers of a militia... In a militia, the character of the labourer, artificer, or tradesman, predominates over that of the soldier... soldiers who are exercised only once a week, or once a-month, can never be so expert... as those who are exercised every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should penalize militias for lower discipline, irregularity, and inferior manual proficiency relative to standing armies; consider frequency of training and occupational conflicts when judging militia effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing army: characteristics and advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of military exercises is the sole or principal occupation of the soldiers of a standing army, and the maintenance or pay which the state affords them is the principal and ordinary fund of their subsistence... a well regulated standing army has [an] irresistible superiority which a well disciplined and well exercised standing army has over a militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standing army yields greater regularity, order, and prompt obedience—qualities decisive in modern warfare—and should be credited for higher battlefield effectiveness when assessing defence options, but also accounted for in fiscal costings and state capacity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological change (fire-arms) shifts the balance toward large-body practice and regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the invention of fire-arms, that army was superior in which the soldiers had, each individually, the greatest skill and dexterity... Since the invention of fire-arms... regularity, order, and prompt obedience to command, are qualities which, in modern armies, are of more importance towards determining the fate of battles, than the dexterity and skill of the soldiers in the use of their arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy judgments must consider weapon-technology: modern weapons increase the value of collective discipline over individual skill, favoring organized, frequently-trained forces (standing armies) in capability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic capacity limits the proportion of population usable as soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: In a civilized society, as the soldiers are maintained altogether by the labour of those who are not soldiers, the number of the former can never exceed what the latter can maintain... it is commonly computed, that not more than the one hundredth part of the inhabitants of any country can be employed as soldiers, without ruin to the country which pays the expense of their service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any defense plan must be constrained by fiscal and productive limits—estimate sustainable troop ratios relative to the productive (non-military) population and assess economic risk of overextension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour and state incentives required to make soldier a profession
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the wisdom of the state only, which can render the trade of a soldier a particular trade, separate and distinct from all others... A private citizen... without any particular encouragement from the public... would not promote his own interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should include state provisioning (pay, pensions, career structure) to professionalize military service; evaluations should check whether such incentives exist if a standing army is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress of manufactures increases the state's cost of defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Those improvements in husbandry, too, which the progress of arts and manufactures necessarily introduces, leave the husbandman as little leisure as the artificer... That wealth... provokes the invasion of all their neighbours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As economies industrialize, policymakers must recognize both increased vulnerability to external predation and higher opportunity costs of mobilizing civilian labour; defence budgets and force structures should reflect these economic transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and regimen of training determine soldier proficiency and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The soldiers, who are exercised only once a week, or once a-month, can never be so expert in the use of their arms, as those who are exercised every day, or every other day... the acknowledged superiority of the Prussian troops, owing, it is said, very much to their superior expertness in their exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing forces, evaluate training schedules and regimen; greater training frequency produces superior manual skill and discipline and should be rewarded in capability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militias serving under their own peacetime leaders perform better
rubrics_metrics.description: Those militias which, like the Tartar or Arab militia, go to war under the same chieftains whom they are accustomed to obey in peace, are by far the best... In respect for their officers, in the habit of ready obedience, they approach nearest to standing armies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs using militia forces should, where possible, preserve peacetime command relationships and local leadership to increase cohesion and obedience, improving effectiveness relative to ad-hoc command arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia may become standing army through repeated campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: A militia of any kind... which has served for several successive campaigns in the field, becomes in every respect a standing army. The soldiers are every day exercised... and... habituated to the same prompt obedience which takes place in standing armies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate transition dynamics: prolonged wartime service can professionalize militias, changing their cost and capability profile; planning should anticipate this evolution and its fiscal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing vs maintaining armies: sequencing of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense of preparing the army for the field seems not to have become considerable in any nation, till long after that of maintaining it in the field had devolved entirely upon the sovereign or commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When budgeting, distinguish between (a) recurrent costs of maintaining troops in the field and (b) peacetime preparation/training costs; in many historical transitions maintaining (paying) troops becomes the larger, earlier fiscal commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal habit and occupation determine readiness for war
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary life, the ordinary exercise of a Tartar or Arab, prepares him sufficiently for war... The necessary occupation of a ditcher prepares him to work in the trenches... The ordinary pastimes of such husbandmen are the same as those of shepherds, and are in the same manner the images of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess population occupations and cultural practices as inputs to mobilization potential: some livelihoods confer transferable skills and readiness that reduce training needs and public cost.
